The paper has three sections: Section A - Physical and General Chemistry (questions 1 and 2); Section B - Inorganic Chemistry (questions 3 and 4); Section C - Organic Chemistry (questions 5 and 6). All six questions are compulsory.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following:

(i) A standard solution.

(ii) A reduction-oxidation (redox) reaction. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Standard solution.** A **standard solution** is a solution whose **concentration is accurately known**. It is prepared by dissolving an accurately weighed mass of a pure substance (a primary standard) in a known volume of solvent, for example in a volumetric flask made up to the mark.

**(ii) Redox reaction.** A **reduction-oxidation (redox) reaction** is a reaction in which **oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously**: one species loses electrons (its oxidation number increases, it is oxidised and acts as the reducing agent) while another species gains those electrons (its oxidation number decreases, it is reduced and acts as the oxidising agent).

questions.enonce_markdown:
A $1.98\ \mathrm{g}$ sample of hydrated oxalic acid ($\mathrm{H_2C_2O_4{\cdot}2H_2O}$, RMM = 126) was dissolved in distilled water and made up to $250\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ in a volumetric flask. $25.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of this solution was acidified and found to react with $30.5\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of $0.021\ \mathrm{M}$ $\mathrm{MnO_4^{-}(aq)}$. Calculate:

(i) Number of moles of $\mathrm{MnO_4^{-}}$ ions that reacted with the $\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}}$ ions.

(ii) Number of moles of $\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}}$ ions in $250\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of the solution. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Moles of permanganate.**

$n(\mathrm{MnO_4^-}) = c \times V = 0.021\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}} \times \dfrac{30.5}{1000}\ \mathrm{dm^3} = 6.405\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{mol}$

**$n(\mathrm{MnO_4^-}) = 6.41\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{mol}$**

**(ii) Moles of oxalate in $250\ \mathrm{cm^3}$.**

Balanced equation (acidic medium):

$5\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}} + 2\mathrm{MnO_4^{-}} + 16\mathrm{H^{+}} \rightarrow 10\mathrm{CO_2} + 2\mathrm{Mn^{2+}} + 8\mathrm{H_2O}$

Mole ratio $\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}} : \mathrm{MnO_4^-} = 5 : 2$, so in the $25.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ aliquot

$n(\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}}) = 6.405\times10^{-4} \times \dfrac{5}{2} = 1.60\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{mol}$.

The aliquot is one tenth of the $250\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ solution, so

$n(\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}})_{250} = 1.60\times10^{-3} \times \dfrac{250}{25.0} = 1.60\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{mol}$.

**Number of moles of $\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}}$ in $250\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ = $0.0160\ \mathrm{mol}$.**

Cross-check from the mass weighed: $\dfrac{1.98}{126} = 0.0157\ \mathrm{mol}$, which agrees with the titration value to within about 2 % (experimental error).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Draw the Born-Haber cycle for the formation of one mole of magnesium oxide.

(ii) Given the following bond energies in $\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$: $E(\mathrm{C{-}H}) = +413$, $E(\mathrm{Cl{-}Cl}) = +242$, $E(\mathrm{C{-}Cl}) = +326$, $E(\mathrm{H{-}Cl}) = +431$. Calculate the enthalpy change for the reaction

$\mathrm{CH_4 + Cl_2 \longrightarrow CH_3Cl + HCl}$ *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Born-Haber cycle for magnesium oxide, $\mathrm{MgO}$.** The cycle links the enthalpy of formation of the solid to the steps that build the ionic lattice from the gaseous ions (Hess's law). The question gives no data and asks only for the drawing, so the cycle is drawn with typical data-book values in $\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ (energy increases upwards):

```
 Mg2+(g) + O2-(g) ------------------------------+
      ^                                         |
      | (6) 2nd electron affinity of O   +798   |
 Mg2+(g) + O-(g) + e-                           |
      ^                                         |
      | (5) 1st electron affinity of O   -141   |
 Mg2+(g) + O(g) + 2e-                           |  (7) lattice
      ^                                         |  formation
      | (4) 1/2 O2(g) -> O(g)            +249   |  enthalpy
 Mg2+(g) + 1/2 O2(g) + 2e-                      |  (negative)
      ^                                         |
      | (2)+(3) 1st + 2nd ionisation     +738   |
      |         energies of Mg          +1451   |
 Mg(g) + 1/2 O2(g)                              |
      ^                                         |
      | (1) atomisation of Mg(s)         +148   |
 Mg(s) + 1/2 O2(g) ---- (8) formation -602 ---> MgO(s)
```

Labelled steps: (1) $\mathrm{Mg(s) \rightarrow Mg(g)}$ enthalpy of atomisation; (2) and (3) $\mathrm{Mg(g) \rightarrow Mg^{+}(g) + e^-}$ and $\mathrm{Mg^{+}(g) \rightarrow Mg^{2+}(g) + e^-}$, the first and second ionisation energies; (4) $\tfrac12\mathrm{O_2(g) \rightarrow O(g)}$ atomisation of oxygen; (5) $\mathrm{O(g) + e^- \rightarrow O^-(g)}$ first electron affinity (exothermic); (6) $\mathrm{O^-(g) + e^- \rightarrow O^{2-}(g)}$ second electron affinity (endothermic, because an electron is added to a negative ion); (7) $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}(g) + O^{2-}(g) \rightarrow MgO(s)}$ lattice formation enthalpy; (8) $\mathrm{Mg(s) + \tfrac12 O_2(g) \rightarrow MgO(s)}$ enthalpy of formation.

By Hess's law, $\Delta H_f = \Delta H_{(1)} + \Delta H_{(2)} + \Delta H_{(3)} + \Delta H_{(4)} + \Delta H_{(5)} + \Delta H_{(6)} + \Delta H_{L}$. With the values above the sum of steps (1) to (6) is $+3243\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$, so $\Delta H_L = -602 - 3243 = -3845\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ (the data-book value is about $-3800$).

**(ii) Enthalpy change of chlorination of methane.**

Bonds broken (energy absorbed): four $\mathrm{C{-}H}$ and one $\mathrm{Cl{-}Cl}$:
$4 \times 413 + 242 = 1652 + 242 = +1894\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$.

Bonds formed (energy released): three $\mathrm{C{-}H}$ (in $\mathrm{CH_3Cl}$), one $\mathrm{C{-}Cl}$ and one $\mathrm{H{-}Cl}$:
$3 \times 413 + 326 + 431 = 1239 + 757 = 1996\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$.

$\Delta H = \sum E(\text{bonds broken}) - \sum E(\text{bonds formed}) = 1894 - 1996$

**$\Delta H = -102\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$** (exothermic). Shortcut: only one $\mathrm{C{-}H}$ and the $\mathrm{Cl{-}Cl}$ bond are broken and the $\mathrm{C{-}Cl}$ and $\mathrm{H{-}Cl}$ bonds formed: $413 + 242 - 326 - 431 = -102$.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the difference between a crystal structure and a unit cell? *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- A **crystal structure** is the **complete, three-dimensional, regularly repeating arrangement of the particles (atoms, ions or molecules)** throughout the whole solid (the crystal lattice with the particles at its points).
- A **unit cell** is the **smallest repeating part (smallest block) of that lattice** which, when repeated in all three directions by translation only, builds up the whole crystal structure. It shows the geometry and the number of particles per repeating unit (for example simple cubic, body-centred cubic, face-centred cubic).

In short: the unit cell is the small repeating unit; the crystal structure is the entire pattern obtained by stacking many unit cells.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The reaction: $\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons NH_3(g)}$  $\Delta H = -92\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ is in equilibrium at $600^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. If the partial pressures of $\mathrm{N_2}$, $\mathrm{H_2}$ and $\mathrm{NH_3}$ are $1.27$, $0.39$ and $0.18\ \mathrm{atm}$ respectively.

*(The equation is printed unbalanced; the balanced reaction is $\mathrm{N_2 + 3H_2 \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3}$.)*

(i) Write an expression for the equilibrium constant, $K_p$ for the reaction.

(ii) Calculate the equilibrium constant, $K_p$ stating its units. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Balanced equation (the value $\Delta H = -92\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ corresponds to the formation of $2\ \mathrm{mol}$ of $\mathrm{NH_3}$):

$\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)}$

**(i) Expression for $K_p$.**

$K_p = \dfrac{(p_{\mathrm{NH_3}})^2}{p_{\mathrm{N_2}} \times (p_{\mathrm{H_2}})^3}$

**(ii) Calculation.**

$K_p = \dfrac{(0.18)^2}{1.27 \times (0.39)^3} = \dfrac{0.0324}{1.27 \times 0.0593} = \dfrac{0.0324}{0.0753} = 0.430$

Units: $\dfrac{\mathrm{atm}^2}{\mathrm{atm} \times \mathrm{atm}^3} = \mathrm{atm^{-2}}$.

**$K_p = 0.43\ \mathrm{atm^{-2}}$** (3 significant figures: $0.430\ \mathrm{atm^{-2}}$).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the conjugate acid / base pairs in the reaction below.

$\mathrm{CH_3NH_2 + H_2O \longrightarrow CH_3NH_3^{+} + OH^{-}}$ *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the Bronsted-Lowry theory an acid donates a proton and a base accepts one. In the reaction (which is in fact reversible):

- $\mathrm{H_2O}$ **gives a proton**, so it is the **acid**; the species left after the loss of the proton, **$\mathrm{OH^-}$**, is its **conjugate base**. Pair 1: $\mathrm{H_2O}$ (acid) / $\mathrm{OH^-}$ (conjugate base).
- $\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$ **accepts a proton**, so it is the **base**; the species formed, **$\mathrm{CH_3NH_3^+}$**, is its **conjugate acid**. Pair 2: $\mathrm{CH_3NH_3^+}$ (acid) / $\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$ (conjugate base).

The two pairs differ by one proton $\mathrm{H^+}$ each.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given the following half-cell reactions and their electrode potentials:

$\mathrm{Cr^{3+}(aq) + e^- \rightleftharpoons Cr^{2+}(aq)}$  $-0.41\ \mathrm{V}$

$\mathrm{MnO_4^{-}(aq) + 8H^{+}(aq) + 5e^- \rightleftharpoons Mn^{2+}(aq) + 4H_2O(l)}$  $+1.52\ \mathrm{V}$

Write the cell diagram and calculate the emf of the cell. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The couple with the more positive $E^{\ominus}$ ($\mathrm{MnO_4^-/Mn^{2+}}$, $+1.52\ \mathrm{V}$) is reduced and is the **positive electrode**; the couple with the more negative $E^{\ominus}$ ($\mathrm{Cr^{3+}/Cr^{2+}}$, $-0.41\ \mathrm{V}$) runs in reverse (oxidation) and is the **negative electrode**.

Negative electrode (oxidation): $\mathrm{Cr^{2+} \rightarrow Cr^{3+} + e^-}$ (multiplied by 5)

Positive electrode (reduction): $\mathrm{MnO_4^{-} + 8H^{+} + 5e^- \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + 4H_2O}$

Overall: $\mathrm{MnO_4^{-} + 8H^{+} + 5Cr^{2+} \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + 5Cr^{3+} + 4H_2O}$

**Cell diagram** (oxidation on the left, reduction on the right; platinum electrodes because both couples are in solution):

$$\mathrm{Pt\,|\,Cr^{2+}(aq),\,Cr^{3+}(aq)\,\|\,MnO_4^{-}(aq),\,H^{+}(aq),\,Mn^{2+}(aq)\,|\,Pt}$$

**emf:** $E_{\text{cell}} = E^{\ominus}_{\text{positive}} - E^{\ominus}_{\text{negative}} = +1.52 - (-0.41) = \mathbf{+1.93\ V}$ (positive, so the reaction is feasible).
